message.content:
I don’t have real‑time data, but you can quickly check the current air quality in Los Angeles by visiting one of the following resources:

| Source | What it offers | How to use |
|--------|----------------|------------|
| **AirNow** (airnow.gov) | Official EPA air‑quality index (AQI) for all U.S. cities, plus pollutant breakdowns (PM₂.₅, PM₁₀, O₃, NO₂, CO). | Enter “Los Angeles” or your ZIP code in the search bar. |
| **AQICN** (aqicn.org) | Global AQI map with real‑time data from local monitoring stations. | Search “Los Angeles” or use the map. |
| **Local news sites** (e.g., LA Times, KABC) | Often publish daily air‑quality summaries and health advisories. | Look for “air quality” or “AQI” in the search bar. |
| **Weather apps** (Weather.com, AccuWeather, Weather Underground) | Many include an AQI widget. | Open the app, search for Los Angeles, and scroll to the “Air Quality” section. |

**Quick tip:** If the AQI is 100–150, it’s “Moderate” – people with respiratory issues might want to limit outdoor activity. Above 150 is “Unhealthy for Sensitive Groups,” and above 200 is “Unhealthy.”  

If you need a more detailed breakdown (e.g., PM₂.₅ concentration, ozone levels), the AirNow website provides that information directly.
